A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Breaking Neural Network Scaling Laws with Modularity. All 29 pages in each version, including Appendices A–F, are readable, and the equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network experiments on linear and nonlinear sine-wave regression and Compositional CIFAR-10, including generalization comparisons, ablations, and distribution-shift tests in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their quantitative results, including Figures 2–5, Tables 2–4, and the supplementary analyses in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The kernel-based module initialization objective, Algorithm 1, subsequent task training, and modular architectures are unchanged. The expanded model explanation in Section 3.1 does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same linear and nonlinear sine-wave tasks and Compositional CIFAR-10 scenarios, including unseen class combinations and noisy training inputs. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 4 and Tables 2–4 retain the same monolithic and randomly initialized modular baselines. Figure 9 also retains the same true-module and fixed-initialization comparisons. The added mixture-of-experts citation is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E retains the same data construction, splits, sample sizes, metrics, architecture configurations, training budgets, and binary-search procedure for sample complexity. The class-combination and noise-test protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter analyses, module-initialization ablations, module-count sensitivity, learned-module visualizations, and out-of-distribution tests are retained unchanged in Appendix F. The expanded discussion introduces no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed reporting in Figure 4, five-trial standard errors in Tables 2–3, four-trial standard errors in Table 4, and five-seed standard deviations in Figure 9. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains the proposed method's test loss of 0.393 ± 0.099, and Table 3 retains accuracies of 42.56%, 45.26%, and 49.90% for the monolithic baseline, modular baseline, and proposed method.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and the derivations in Appendices A–D are unchanged. Section 3.1's explanation of matrix-valued features and vector-valued parameters already appeared in v1's Appendix A.1. Displaying y(x) = φ(x)W separately and renumbering equations introduces no new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal discussion claims retain the same theoretical sample-complexity advantage under the stated modular assumptions and the same empirical generalization claims. The scope of the central contributions is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds an explicit inference that optimization beyond ordinary gradient descent may unlock further generalization benefits in routing, attention, and mixture-of-experts architectures. Its additional self-attention sentence reinforces speculation already present in v1. The substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same kernels, architecture specifications, hyperparameter sweeps, optimization settings, GPU memory information, and Algorithms 1–2. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jacobs et al. (1991), Adaptive mixtures of local experts, alongside Shazeer et al. (2017) in Section 4.1 and the references. This modestly expands historical attribution without revising the paper's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 incorporates an explanation previously confined to Appendix A.1 and clarifies the feature assumptions. v2 also makes small wording corrections, expands Section 5, and updates the publication header. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 reduces the size of Table 1 and Figure 1 and adjusts main-text spacing and the positions of existing displays. All twelve figures and four tables are retained with unchanged content; the appendix layouts are effectively unchanged.

improvement.justification: The expanded Section 3.1 makes the model setup easier to understand without consulting Appendix A.1, and the added citation improves historical attribution. These are modest improvements in exposition and context; the scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged. Smaller rendering of Table 1 and Figure 1 slightly reduces legibility but does not outweigh those gains.
